results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
I built this as a **four-color control brew**: a Jeskai control deck with a light black splash so it can cast Inevitable Defeat. The legality check passed with no errors or warnings, and the deck was accepted.

**The plan:** Use cheap spells to survive early: Lightning Helix, No More Lies, Spell Snare, Get Lost. On turn 4, land Resonating Lute. With Lute out, every land taps for two mana of any one color for instants and sorceries. That makes Jeskai Revelation (7 mana) castable from turn 5. It also fixes the black for Inevitable Defeat, which exiles any nonland permanent, can't be countered and drains 3. Card draw like Stock Up and Consult the Star Charts keeps your hand at 7+, so Lute can also tap to draw. The deck wins slowly, mostly through Revelation's damage, Monk tokens and drain effects, around turn 9 or later.

**Main deck (60)**
- 3 Resonating Lute, 4 Inevitable Defeat, 3 Jeskai Revelation
- 4 Lightning Helix, 2 Get Lost, 2 Day of Judgment, 1 Seam Rip
- 4 No More Lies, 2 Spell Snare, 1 Three Steps Ahead
- 4 Consult the Star Charts, 4 Stock Up
- **Lands (26):** 4 Great Hall of the Biblioplex, 4 Hallowed Fountain, 4 Steam Vents, 2 Sacred Foundry, 2 Godless Shrine, 1 Watery Grave, 3 Floodfarm Verge, 1 Sunbillow Verge, 1 Riverpyre Verge, 2 Starting Town, 1 Meticulous Archive, 1 Multiversal Passage

**Sideboard (15):** 2 Pyroclasm, 1 Fire Magic, 2 Negate, 2 Disdainful Stroke, 2 Duress, 2 Tishana's Tidebinder, 1 Wan Shi Tong, Librarian, 1 The Unagi of Kyoshi Island, 1 Seam Rip, 1 Rest in Peace

**Why these cards**
- **Lute is already proven.** The most recent 5-0 Jeskai Control league list ran 3 Lute and 3 Revelation. I took that list's mana and interaction, then swapped its 2 Flashback, extra Get Lost, extra Seam Rip and a Three Steps Ahead for 4 Inevitable Defeat.
- **Inevitable Defeat** shows up almost only in rogue lists (28 lists in 90 days), so the splash is the new part.
- **Great Hall of the Biblioplex** taps for any color, for 1 life, but that mana only casts instants and sorceries. Defeat is an instant, so all four Great Halls count as black sources. Lute helps the same way.

**The mana**
- 26 lands, matching the Jeskai Control average of 26.1.
- Sources: 19 white, 20 blue, 14 red, 9 black. The Jeskai Control averages are 17 white, 18 blue and 12.6 red.
- Black comes from 4 Great Hall, 2 Godless Shrine, 1 Watery Grave, 2 Starting Town and the Passage (set to Swamp).
- Counting the 3 Lutes, you have a black source or a Lute by turn 5 93.4% of the time.
- You draw a Lute naturally by turn 5 only 46.2% of the time. The 8 card-selection spells push that higher, but the deck has to work without Lute too.

**Sideboarding against the field**
- **Prowess (20.8%), Boros and Elementals:** bring in Pyroclasm, Fire Magic and the second Seam Rip. Take out Three Steps Ahead, a Stock Up and a Lute.
- **Dimir Excruciator, Dimir Midrange and Lessons:** bring in Negate, Duress, Tidebinder, Wan Shi Tong and Unagi. Take out Day of Judgment, Seam Rip and some Helix.
- **Big-spell decks (Simic Omniscience, Landfall payoffs):** Disdainful Stroke.
- **Graveyard decks:** Rest in Peace.
- **Landfall (15.6%):** Tidebinder can stop triggers, and Defeat answers payoffs.

**Not verified**
- No one has tested this exact four-color build. The win turn is an estimate, not a result.
- Great Hall makes only colorless mana for Lute and Day of Judgment, and its colored mana costs 1 life. Fast red decks may punish that, along with the shocklands.
- Duress is a sorcery, so Great Hall and Lute can pay for it. Even so, sideboarding it in strains the black more than the main deck does.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
This is a four-color (G/W/U/R) creature ramp deck where The Jolly Balloon Man copies your best creature each turn. You ramp with mana dorks, and Bloom Tender turns into a four-mana creature once Balloon Man (red and white) and Cam (blue) are out. Then you hard-cast or tutor up Craterhoof Behemoth and use Cam to untap Balloon Man so it copies the Hoof too. That gives your team two +X/+X pumps for a turn-5 kill.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves
- 3 Gene Pollinator
- 4 Bloom Tender
- 2 Spider Manifestation
- 4 The Jolly Balloon Man
- 3 Brightglass Gearhulk
- 2 Glamermite
- 1 Formidable Speaker
- 1 Mockingbird
- 3 Ouroboroid
- 2 Craterhoof Behemoth
- 4 Sewer-veillance Cam
- 3 Nature's Rhythm
- 2 Seam Rip
- 22 lands: 4 Temple Garden, 4 Hushwood Verge, 3 Breeding Pool, 2 Stomping Ground, 2 Sacred Foundry, 3 Starting Town, 1 Thornspire Verge, 1 Botanical Sanctum, 2 Forest

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Get Lost
- 2 Meltstrider's Resolve
- 2 Pawpatch Formation
- 2 Disdainful Stroke
- 2 Surrak, Elusive Hunter
- 1 Beza, the Bounding Spring
- 2 Rest in Peace
- 1 Soul-Guide Lantern

**How the three cards work together**
- **The Jolly Balloon Man:** For {1} and tapping, it makes a 1/1 flying, hasty copy of another creature you control. You sacrifice the copy at the end step, and you can only do this at sorcery speed. Because the copy has haste, it can be a creature you use right away. The best targets:
  - **Bloom Tender:** The copy taps right away for about +3 mana.
  - **Craterhoof Behemoth:** The copy pumps your team a second time.
  - **Brightglass Gearhulk:** The copy tutors two more cards with mana value 1 or less.
  - **Glamermite:** The copy untaps Balloon Man so it can go again.
- **Sewer-veillance Cam:** It costs {U}, has flash, and can tap or untap a creature both when it enters and when it leaves. Later you can pay {3}{U} and sacrifice it to draw two, which also triggers the untap again. Use it to:
  - untap Balloon Man for a second copy in the same turn,
  - untap Bloom Tender for another big tap of mana, or
  - tap down a blocker.
- **Bloom Tender:** It makes one mana of each color among your permanents. The deck spreads its colors out on purpose so Tender makes three or four mana: Balloon Man is red and white, Cam and Glamermite are blue, and Spider Manifestation and Gearhulk add more colors.
- **Support cards:**
  - Brightglass Gearhulk can tutor Cam, Elves, Pollinator, Seam Rip or Mockingbird.
  - Nature's Rhythm and Formidable Speaker find Craterhoof.
  - Ouroboroid is a second way to win over a longer game.

**I checked for an infinite combo, and there isn't one.** Copying Glamermite or North Pole Patrol untaps Balloon Man, but each loop costs {1} and gives back only one untap. You can't untap Balloon Man and also make mana in the same loop. With a lot of mana, Balloon Man plus Glamermite makes a swarm of hasty fliers that Hoof then pumps, but the number is limited by your mana.

**Odds (without mulligans):**
- By turn 3, you have a mana creature 91% of the time and Balloon Man 49% of the time.
- By turn 5, you've seen Hoof or Nature's Rhythm 65% of the time, and Cam or a Gearhulk to find it 78% of the time.

Formidable Speaker and Mockingbird are extra ways to find or copy Hoof.

**Mana:** I copied the Aang deck's mana base, since it's the proven green creature-ramp deck with Craterhoof, and added red. There are 22 lands, about 23 green sources, 14–15 white, 9–10 red and 8–9 blue. Gene Pollinator, Starting Town and Bloom Tender make any color you need. The deck check found no problems compared with real Aang lists.

**Sideboarding**
- **Against Prowess (28% of the meta) and Selesnya Offense:** Bring in Get Lost, Meltstrider's Resolve, Beza and Surrak. Take out Ouroboroid, Mockingbird and a Formidable Speaker. Your mana creatures die to burn, so be ready to slow down and play as a midrange deck.
- **Against Lessons, 4C Control and Dimir Excruciator:** Bring in Disdainful Stroke, which counters spells with mana value 4 or more, and Surrak, which can't be countered and draws you a card when they target your creatures. Take out Seam Rip.
- **Against Azorius Skies:** Bring in Pawpatch Formation, which can destroy a flier.
- **Against Reanimator:** Bring in Rest in Peace and Soul-Guide Lantern. Keep in mind Rest in Peace also exiles your own graveyard, so you lose Nature's Rhythm's second cast from the graveyard.

**Label:** This is a **brew**. It borrows its mana base and its Craterhoof/Gearhulk package from Aang, but the engine is new. Balloon Man has no recent tournament results, and Cam and Bloom Tender show up in only a handful of lists.

**Caveats:**
- Badgermole Cub is **banned**, so I left it out, even though it's in nearly every Aang list.
- Leyline Weaver didn't come up when I looked it up, so I didn't use it.

**Main deck (60)**
*Creatures (24), all Dwarves*
- 4 Dwarven Mauler
- 2 Bofur, Reliable Guardian
- 4 Kíli the Resourceful
- 4 Dáin's Company
- 3 Thorin Oakenshield
- 3 Giott, King of the Dwarves
- 2 Dáin Ironfoot
- 2 Fíli the Pathfinder

*Equipment (8)*

- 2 Lost Jitte
- 2 Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor

*Spells (6)*

- 2 Lightning Helix

*Lands (22)*

- 4 Sunbillow Verge

- 3 Mountain
- 3 Plains

- 3 Magebane Lizard
- 3 Sear
- 2 Ghost Vacuum
- 2 Rest in Peace
- 2 Get Lost
- 2 Abrade
- 1 Shattered Acolyte

**The plan**
Play cheap Dwarves early, put equipment on them, and keep drawing cards so you don't run out of attackers. Kíli draws a card once each turn when another Dwarf or an Equipment enters. Dáin's Company finds your next threat. Giott, Dáin Ironfoot and Mjölnir turn one equipped creature into a lot of damage. The goal is to win around turn 6.

**Why these cards**
- **Dwarven Mauler:** costs 1 mana, and its equip costs are 2 less. Mattock's equip {3} becomes {1}, and Jitte's {1} becomes free.
- **Kíli the Resourceful:**
  - Every creature in the deck is a Dwarf, and there are 8 Equipment, so the draw triggers almost every turn.
  - Its free-equip bonus needs 3 or more artifacts and/or legendaries. That comes quickly: Kíli itself, Thorin, Giott, Bofur, Dáin, Fíli, Lost Jitte, Mjölnir, Mattock and Dáin's Axe token all count.
- **Dáin's Company:** 32 of the 60 cards are a Dwarf or an Equipment it can find, so its look at the top four almost always hits. It also has lifelink whenever you control another Dwarf, which is almost always.
- **Dwarven Mattock:** attaches itself to a Dwarf for free when it enters and gives +2/+2 and ward 1.
- **Giott:** has double strike, so any equipment on it counts twice.
- **Dáin Ironfoot:** makes an equipment token when it enters (which also triggers Kíli). When it attacks, every equipped attacker gets double strike.
- **Mjölnir:** deals 4 damage to a creature when it enters. It equips for just 1 onto a legendary red or white creature (Kíli, Thorin, Giott, Bofur), and it doubles that creature's damage.
- **Fíli the Pathfinder:** makes a 2/2 Dwarf token whenever it or another real Dwarf enters, and gives your team +1/+1 once you have the 3 artifacts/legendaries.
- **Thorin Oakenshield:** with the same condition met, gives your creatures and artifacts ward 1.
- **Burst Lightning and Lightning Helix:** clear early blockers or finish the opponent.
- **Odds:** on the play, you have about a 49% chance to see Kíli by turn 3. You have about an 89% chance to see a Mattock, Jitte, Mjölnir or Dáin's Company that can feed it.

**The mana**
I based the mana on the Boros Aggro decks in recent results, adjusted for a two-color deck. Those decks average about 23 lands. This one runs 22 because almost nothing costs more than 2 (average mana value 1.95). That gives 19 red sources and 17 white sources. The Lonely Mountain is a red land that enters untapped once you have an equipment out. Late in the game it makes 2/2 Dwarves, which also trigger Kíli and Fíli.

**Sideboarding**
- **Prowess (21.7% of the field):** bring in 3 Magebane Lizard and 3 Sear. Take out 2 Mjölnir, 2 Fíli and 2 Lost Jitte.
- **Lessons, Elementals and Reanimator:** bring in 2 Ghost Vacuum and 2 Rest in Peace. Take out 2 Lightning Helix and 2 Fíli.
- **Selesnya Offense and Landfall:** bring in Get Lost, Sear and Abrade. Take out Bofur and Fíli.
- **4C Control and Dimir Excruciator:** keep the threats. Bring in Get Lost and Shattered Acolyte for their artifacts and enchantments. Take out Lightning Helix.

**What I couldn't check**
- The tools had no tournament results for these Dwarves, so how well the deck matches up is my estimate.
- The sideboard plans come from what the most-played decks run, not from games played with this deck.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built this as an Orzhov (white-black) aristocrats deck, which means it sacrifices its own creatures for value. The cheap creatures leave something behind when they die, and the three cards you asked for turn each sacrifice into card selection, mana and lost life for the opponent. It's a **brew**. None of the three cards shows up as a core card in recent Standard results: Sackville and Zealot each appear in one list, and Freebooter in none.

**The plan**
- **Turns 1–2:** Play cheap creatures that are worth sacrificing, then a free sacrifice outlet. With 9 outlets and 12 one-drops plus Bloodghast, you have both by turn 3 about 70% of the time on the play.
- **From turn 3:** Drain the opponent 1 life at a time with The Sackville-Bagginses, push damage with Voice of Victory and Vito, and finish with Bloodghast's haste or Vito's 4/3 fliers.
- **Where I expect the win:** around turn 6.

**Why these cards**
- **Greedy Freebooter (4 copies):** A 1-mana creature that dies into a scry and a Treasure. The Treasure is a token, so sacrificing it later with Sackville in play drains 1 more life.
- **Umbral Collar Zealot (4):** Sacrifices for free, at instant speed. It answers removal and steal effects, and it surveils to set up your draws. Bartolomé del Presidio (2) is a second free outlet that grows with each sacrifice.
- **The Sackville-Bagginses (3):** Its enter-the-battlefield sacrifice draws a card and makes a Treasure. After that, every token you sacrifice costs the opponent 1 life. It's legendary, so I run 3.
- **Token makers for Sackville:**
  - Nesting Bot dies into a 1/1 Servo token.
  - Tolls of War makes a Clue, then a 1/1 Ally token each turn you sacrifice something.
  - Voice of Victory makes two attacking 1/1 Warrior tokens each time it attacks, and you have to sacrifice them at end of turn. With Sackville out, that's 2 free drains per attack. Voice also stops opponents from casting spells during your turn.
- **Bloodghast (4):** Comes back from the graveyard whenever a land enters under your control, so you can sacrifice it again and again.
- **Vito (3):** Rewards three sacrifices in one turn: gain 2 life, drain 2, then make a 4/3 flier.
- **Removal (8):** Requiting Hex, Erode, Bitter Triumph and Get Lost. Requiting Hex's optional -1/-1 counter can go on a 1/1 like Freebooter to cash it in on purpose, which also gets you the 2 life.

**Mana**
- 22 lands, with 21 black and 20 white sources. That's in line with the Lifegain deck's mana, which I borrowed, and check_deck found no issues.
- I added extra black sources because Bloodghast costs BB.
- Starting Town can make colored mana by paying 1 life, and all the lands help bring back Bloodghast.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Prowess (17%) and Selesnya Offense:** bring in 2 Seam Rip and 2 Deep-Cavern Bat. Take out the Tolls of War and 1 Vito.
- **Landfall and Elementals:** bring in 2 Pyrrhic Strike and Get Lost against their bigger threats. Trim Bartolomé.
- **Lessons, 4C Control and Dimir Excruciator:** bring in 2 Duress and 2 Deep-Cavern Bat. Cut Erode and Requiting Hex, which have fewer good targets there. Voice of Victory is already strong against counterspells.
- **Reanimator:** bring in 2 Leyline of the Void, 2 Ghost Vacuum and 2 Strategic Betrayal. Ghost Vacuum is also an artifact you can sacrifice.

**What I couldn't verify**
- All the card text and legality above comes from the card database. But this exact list has never been tested in recorded results, so how it does against the field is a projection.
- The 69.5% figure is with no mulligans.
- One weakness: Pest Control (4C Control runs it in about 163 lists) destroys every nonland permanent with mana value 1 or less, including your one-drops and tokens. Against 4C Control, hold back some fodder instead of playing it all out.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
The deck is submitted and legal. This is a **brew**, not a stock list. Gideon's Memorial and Solitary Cell each showed up in just one list over the last 90 days, and Ajani Unrelenting in five, so no proven version of this exists yet.

## The plan
This is Boros "Superfriends": a deck built on lots of planeswalkers. Solitary Cell and burn handle early threats, and Gideon's Memorial speeds out your walkers a turn early. Ajani Unrelenting is the payoff. It makes a 2/2 Cadet token **every time you activate any loyalty ability**, so each walker you control turns into a Cadet factory. Its −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens, and its +1 gives the token army +1/+0 and haste to finish the game.

## Why the key cards
- **Gideon's Memorial (4):** Its mana only casts planeswalkers, and the deck runs 14 of them. Turn 2 Memorial means a 4-mana Chandra on turn 3, or Ajani Unrelenting on turn 5. It also gives tokens +1/+0 and vigilance, and you can discard it for {1}{W} to deal 4 damage to an attacking or blocking creature. It can't pay for the "Way" enchantments, since they aren't planeswalkers.
- **Solitary Cell (4):** Turn-2 removal that exiles a permanent with mana value 3 or less. Later, it draws cards by discarding a legendary card. 22 of the main-deck cards are legendary (all the walkers, the Ways and the Memorial), so spare copies always have a use.
- **Ajani Unrelenting (4):** With 4 copies you have about a 60% chance of seeing one by turn 6 on the play. Some form of planeswalker shows up by turn 4 about 95% of the time.
- **Extra loyalty activations:**
  - **Ajani, Outland Chaperone:** Makes a 1/1 every turn or kills a tapped creature.
  - **Chandra, Torch of Defiance:** Draws cards, ramps or deals 4 to a creature.
  - **Elspeth, Storm Slayer:** Doubles every token you make, so each activation gives you **two** Cadets.
  - **Way of the Healer and Way of the Warlord:** Each makes a Jace token with 5 loyalty, which is one more walker to activate. Healer gives all your walkers "−2: make a Cadet." Warlord gives them "−4: 2 damage to a creature and 2 to a player."
- **Hexhaven Battalion (1):** Late, it makes three Cadets (six with Elspeth). Early, you can landcycle it for {2} to find a basic land.
- **Removal:** 4 Burst Lightning, 3 Sear and 2 Get Lost keep attackers off your walkers.

## The mana
24 lands, with 18 white and 18 red sources. check_deck recommended about 23.8 lands, and Boros Aggro decks average 22.8. I added a land because this deck tops out at six mana. The Boros Aggro land base is the model: Sacred Foundry, Inspiring Vantage, Sunbillow Verge and Multiversal Passage. I added 2 Dedicated Commons, which come in untapped once you control a planeswalker.

## Sideboarding against the field
- **Jund Sacrifice (15.2%) and Reanimator:** Bring in 3 Rest in Peace. Take out Sear or Get Lost.
- **Elementals, Prowess, Boros Dwarves, Landfall:** Bring in 3 Pyroclasm, 3 Seam Rip and 2 Erode. Take out Hexhaven Battalion, a Way of the Healer and an Elspeth. Pyroclasm also kills your own 1/1s and 2/2s, so cast it before you build a board.
- **Dimir Midrange and the control decks:** Bring in 2 Dawn's Truce to protect walkers from removal and 2 Boros Charm for reach and indestructibility. Take out some burn.
- **Boros Dragons:** Bring in Erode, the main answer to big flyers.

## What I couldn't verify
- None of the "Way of" enchantments, Dedicated Commons or Hexhaven Battalion have tournament results yet, so how well they perform is untested.
- Elspeth's token doubling probably also creates two Jace tokens when you empower Jace. The legend rule then makes you keep only one, so that part of the doubling is wasted. This is my reading of the rules, not something the tools confirmed.
- I left out Clarion Conqueror even though Boros Dragons plays it. It stops activated abilities of planeswalkers, which would shut down your whole deck.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Slumbering Trudge, Fight Rigging and The Great Henge.
results.text:
**Mono-Green "Sleeping Giants" (Pioneer brew)**

**Plan:** The idea that makes this deck work is that Slumbering Trudge doesn't need to untap. If you cast it for X=0, you get a tapped 6/6 for one green mana, and that 6 power counts right away. The Great Henge costs less based on your biggest creature's power, so with Trudge out it costs 3 mana. Fight Rigging only checks whether you control a creature with 7 or more power, and its first +1/+1 counter takes Trudge to 7. That turns on a free hidden card every combat. Ghalta, Primal Hunger and the 6/6 bodies then end the game.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Elvish Mystic
- 4 Slumbering Trudge, 4 Pugnacious Hammerskull, 3 Rhonas the Indomitable
- 2 Formidable Speaker, 2 Ghalta, Primal Hunger, 1 Vaultborn Tyrant
- 4 Fight Rigging, 3 The Great Henge
- 4 Hunter's Talent, 2 Biosynthic Burst, 2 Snakeskin Veil
- 15 Forest, 2 Lair of the Hydra, 2 Boseiju, Who Endures, 2 Castle Garenbrig

**Why these cards**
- **Pugnacious Hammerskull (a 6/6 for 3) and Rhonas (a 5/5 for 3):** These back up Trudge as cheap big bodies, so Henge stays at 3–4 mana. Hammerskull only gets a stun counter when it attacks without another Dinosaur, and Ghalta and Vaultborn Tyrant are both Dinosaurs. Rhonas can attack once Trudge or Hammerskull is out. Its +2/+0 pump can be used while Fight Rigging's trigger is waiting to resolve, which gets a 5-power creature to 7.
- **Ghalta:** It costs less based on the total power of your creatures. Trudge plus Hammerskull is 12 power, so Ghalta costs just GG.
- **Pump spells and untappers:** Snakeskin Veil and Biosynthic Burst add a +1/+1 counter, so they also reach the 7-power mark, and they protect your threat. Untapping a stunned creature removes a stun counter instead, so Biosynthic Burst and Formidable Speaker wake Trudge up early. Formidable Speaker can also search out Trudge or Ghalta.
- **Hunter's Talent:** Your creature deals damage equal to its power, so with a 6/6 out it kills almost anything for 2 mana. That makes it the deck's main removal.
- **Speed:** By turn 3 on the play, you see a cheap big body 86% of the time, Rigging or Henge 70%, and both together 59%.

**Mana:** I copied the land count of the real Mono-Green Devotion lists (they average 21.1 lands): 21 lands, all 25 sources green, plus 8 one-mana elves. The deck checker suggests about 24 lands. I think 21 is enough, because Henge and Ghalta are almost never cast at full price, and Castle Garenbrig and Lair of the Hydra give you something to do with spare mana.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Greasefang, Izzet Phoenix, Lessons:** Bring in 2 Soul-Guide Lantern and 2 Unlicensed Hearse, which exile graveyards. Against Greasefang, also add Scrapshooter and Haywire Mite to hit its vehicles. Take out Snakeskin Veil and Formidable Speaker.
- **Golgari Midrange, UW Control, Niv-Mizzet:** Bring in Surrak (can't be countered, and draws a card when they target your creatures), Questing Beast and Tamiyo's Safekeeping. Take out Hunter's Talent against control.
- **Izzet Prowess, Mono-Red Prowess, Selesnya Company:** Bring in Polukranos Reborn and Voracious Hydra, which kill or block their creatures. Cut Vaultborn Tyrant, one Ghalta and Biosynthic Burst.

**Label:** This is a brew. None of the three cards you asked for show up in any recent Pioneer results. I only borrowed the land count and some sideboard ideas from Mono-Green Devotion.

**What I couldn't verify:** There's no tournament data for this deck, so how it does against the field is a guess. Its weak spots are that early removal on Trudge or Hammerskull switches off both Rigging and Henge, and that it plays very few instant-speed answers.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Guiding Voice, Practiced Offense and Favored Hoplite.
results.text:
I built a mono-white Heroic brew where every spell targets your own creatures. Favored Hoplite and its companions grow from turn 1, and the cheap spells that target them also protect them, draw cards or take away blockers. Practiced Offense finishes the job: it puts a counter on your whole team, gives double strike or lifelink to your biggest attacker, and you can cast it again from the graveyard later.

**Main deck (60)**
*Creatures (16)*
- 4 Favored Hoplite
- 4 Illuminator Virtuoso
- 4 Phalanx Leader
- 4 Hero of Iroas

*Spells (24)*
- 4 Guiding Voice
- 4 Honor
- 4 Homestead Courage
- 4 Gods Willing
- 4 Sheltered by Ghosts
- 4 Practiced Offense

*Lands (20)*
- 15 Plains
- 2 Eiganjo, Seat of the Empire
- 2 Idyllic Grange
- 1 Sejiri Shelter (a protection spell that can be played as a land)

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Rest in Peace
- 3 Elite Spellbinder
- 3 Portable Hole
- 2 Dawn's Truce
- 2 Get Lost
- 2 Take Up the Shield

**Why these cards**
- **Favored Hoplite:** Each time you target it, it gets a counter and prevents all damage to itself that turn. That makes it a 1-drop that fights well and is hard to kill with damage.
- **Guiding Voice:** A counter plus learn for {W}. This deck has no Lessons, so learn just means "discard a card to draw a card." That turns extra lands into more spells.
- **Practiced Offense:** It targets a player, not a creature, when it hands out counters. But its second target, the creature that gets double strike or lifelink, does set off heroic. The best play is to aim it at Phalanx Leader, which gives your team two rounds of counters. Or aim it at Illuminator Virtuoso, which already has double strike, and give it lifelink.
- **Phalanx Leader:** Its heroic puts a counter on *each* creature you control. Any 1-mana spell aimed at it becomes a team-wide boost. No recent results include it.
- **Illuminator Virtuoso:** A double-striker that draws, then discards a card every time you target it. It's in the Azorius Heroic lists.
- **Hero of Iroas:** Another heroic 2-drop, and it makes Sheltered by Ghosts cost {W}.
- **Spells that target:**
  - Honor draws a card.
  - Homestead Courage can be cast again from the graveyard for {W}, so it's two heroic triggers in one card.
  - Gods Willing is protection.
  - Sheltered by Ghosts is your only main-deck removal, and it also gives lifelink and ward.

With 16 heroic creatures and 24 targeting spells, you have a 93% chance to see a creature by turn 2 on the play, and 92% to see both a creature and a spell.

**Mana**
It's 20 white sources: 19 lands plus Sejiri Shelter. The checker flagged that mono-white lists average 22.8 lands. Those are mostly slower control builds, though. This deck has an average mana value of 1.61, nothing costs more than 3, and Practiced Offense's {1}{W} recast is its only real mana sink. The Azorius Heroic list I borrowed the shell from ran 20 lands, counting its own Sejiri Shelter. Idyllic Grange comes in untapped once you have three other Plains and puts a free counter on a creature. Eiganjo is a land that can also be discarded as removal for an attacker or blocker.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Greasefang (12.5%) and Izzet Phoenix:** Bring in Rest in Peace and Portable Hole. Take out Hero of Iroas and a Gods Willing.
- **Golgari or Dimir Midrange (about 17% combined):**
  - Bring in Elite Spellbinder, Dawn's Truce and Get Lost to strip their removal and answer their threats.
  - Take out Guiding Voice and Hero of Iroas.
- **Selesnya Company:** Bring in Portable Hole and Get Lost. Take out some Gods Willing.
- **Izzet and Mono-Red Prowess (about 18%):** Bring in Take Up the Shield and Portable Hole. Lifelink plus Hoplite's damage prevention is how you beat burn. Take out Guiding Voice.
- **UW Control:** Bring in Elite Spellbinder and Dawn's Truce, which protects your whole board from sweepers if you give them the extra card. Take out Gods Willing, which doesn't stop board wipes, and one Practiced Offense.

**Label:** This is a brew. The mana and the heroic shell come from Azorius Heroic, made mono-white and built around your three cards. Only a couple of recent mono-white lists played all three together.

**Couldn't verify:** I have no win-rate data for this exact build. The deck is very weak to sweepers and to removal cast in response to your spells, so the sideboard plans above are my judgment, not results from tournaments.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery.
results.text:
I've built a 4-color (white, blue, black, red) control deck that plays almost everything at instant speed. It's a brew: Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery showed 0, 0 and 5 recent tournament lists. I borrowed the general shape of UW Control and the multicolor land base of the Niv-Mizzet decks.

**The plan**
Trade 1-for-1 early with burn, removal and counterspells. Tablet of Discovery speeds you up so you can cast Jeskai Revelation at the end of your opponent's turn 5. Then Torrential Gearhulk recasts Revelation or Inevitable Defeat from your graveyard for free. The deck usually takes over around turns 5–7 and wins with Monk tokens, Gearhulk and Wandering Emperor, plus Inevitable Defeat's 3-point drain.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Tablet of Discovery
- 3 Jeskai Revelation
- 3 Inevitable Defeat
- 2 Torrential Gearhulk
- 4 Lightning Helix
- 3 Get Lost
- 3 Leyline Binding
- 3 No More Lies
- 1 Dovin's Veto
- 3 Consult the Star Charts
- 2 The Wandering Emperor
- 2 Deafening Clarion
- 1 Supreme Verdict
- 26 lands:
  - 2 Raugrin Triome, 2 Raffine's Tower, 1 Xander's Lounge, 1 Savai Triome
  - 2 Hallowed Fountain, 2 Sacred Foundry, 1 Steam Vents, 1 Watery Grave, 1 Godless Shrine
  - 2 Fabled Passage
  - 2 Floodfarm Verge, 2 Sunbillow Verge, 1 Bleachbone Verge, 1 Riverpyre Verge
  - 1 Plains, 2 Island, 1 Mountain, 1 Swamp

**Sideboard (15)**
- 2 Rest in Peace
- 2 Dovin's Veto
- 2 Torch the Tower
- 2 Temporary Lockdown
- 1 Supreme Verdict
- 2 Beza, the Bounding Spring
- 1 Teferi, Hero of Dominaria
- 1 Sphinx's Revelation
- 2 Kolaghan's Command

**Why these cards**
- **Tablet of Discovery:** It taps for R, or RR that can only be spent on instants and sorceries. That's not a real limit here, since 19 of the main-deck cards are instants. Five lands plus Tablet pays for Revelation's seven mana. Its "mill a card, you may play it" also gives you an extra card.
- **Jeskai Revelation:** One card that does five things: bounces a spell or permanent, deals 4 damage, makes two 1/1 Monks with prowess, draws two and gains 4 life. It's an instant, so you cast it at the end of their turn.
- **Inevitable Defeat:** It can't be countered and exiles any nonland permanent. That covers what Get Lost misses (artifacts, vehicles), and it's your answer to UW Control's counterspells. The drain also helps you close.
- **Torrential Gearhulk:** It has flash and casts an instant from your graveyard for free. On Revelation or Defeat, that's the second copy of your best spell plus a 5/6 body.
- **Support:** Lightning Helix, Get Lost and the two sweepers (Deafening Clarion, Supreme Verdict) keep you alive. Leyline Binding costs only 2 mana once your lands cover four basic land types (the triomes and shocks do this). No More Lies, Dovin's Veto and Consult the Star Charts round out the instant suite.

**The mana**
- 26 lands, which matches the deck checker's recommendation (26.7).
- Colored sources: white 18, blue 16, red 13 plus 4 Tablets, black 10 (counting Fabled Passage, which can fetch the Swamp).
- Black is kept light on purpose: Inevitable Defeat is the only black card in the main deck, which is why I chose Get Lost over Vanishing Verse.
- The deck checker compared this to the Niv-Mizzet decks and flagged fewer lands and black/red sources. Those are 80-card, five-color lists, so the raw numbers don't carry over. 26 of 60 is the same share as their 35 of 80.

**Odds:** By turn 5 on the play, you'll have seen Revelation or Gearhulk 65% of the time and a Tablet 57% of the time. Both together happen only 36% of the time, so expect a Revelation turn closer to 6–7 in many games.

**Sideboarding against the top decks**
- **Mono-Red / Izzet Prowess (about 20% of the field):** Bring in 2 Temporary Lockdown, 2 Torch the Tower, 2 Beza and 1 Supreme Verdict. Take out the No More Lies, Dovin's Veto, 2 Consult and 1 Gearhulk.
- **Greasefang (11%):** Bring in 2 Rest in Peace and 2 Kolaghan's Command. Take out 2 Clarion and 2 Consult.
- **Izzet Phoenix (9%):** Bring in 2 Rest in Peace and 2 Torch the Tower. Take out 1 Verdict, 1 Gearhulk and 2 Leyline Binding.
- **Golgari Midrange (13%):** Bring in 1 Supreme Verdict and 2 Beza. Take out 2 Clarion and 1 Veto.
- **UW Control and Lotus Field:** Bring in 2 Dovin's Veto, Teferi and Sphinx's Revelation. Take out the sweepers and 2 Get Lost. Inevitable Defeat can't be countered, so it stays in.

**What I couldn't check:** This exact deck has no tournament results, so its matchups are untested. Its weakest point is the early turns against fast aggro, before Tablet and the sweepers come online.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Tolarian Terror, Bushwhack and Eddymurk Crab.
results.text:
I've built **Simic Serpents**, a Blue-Green tempo deck. It's a brew: no recent Pioneer results show Tolarian Terror or Bushwhack at all, and Eddymurk Crab shows up in only one list (Izzet Crab).

**The plan**
Spend turns 1–3 on 1-mana cantrips and interaction. That fills your graveyard with instants and sorceries, so Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab come down for 1–3 mana as 5/5s around turn 3 or 4. Once a 5/5 is out, your cheap spells become threats: Bushwhack and Ram Through turn it into removal, Snakeskin Veil protects it, and Stubborn Denial becomes a hard counter.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Creatures (14):**
  - 4 Tolarian Terror
  - 4 Eddymurk Crab
  - 4 Ledger Shredder
  - 2 Brazen Borrower
- **Spells (27):**

  - 4 Consider
  - 3 Opt
  - 2 Sleight of Hand
  - 2 Otherworldly Gaze
  - 2 Spell Pierce
  - 2 Stubborn Denial
  - 2 Fading Hope
  - 2 Ram Through
  - 2 Snakeskin Veil
  - 1 Into the Flood Maw
  - 1 Quandrix Charm
- **Lands (19):**
  - 4 Breeding Pool
  - 4 Botanical Sanctum
  - 2 Yavimaya Coast
  - 2 Hinterland Harbor
  - 1 Hedge Maze
  - 4 Island
  - 2 Forest

**Why these cards**
- **Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab:** Each costs {1} less for every instant or sorcery in your graveyard. Terror has ward 2. The Crab has flash, and when it enters it taps up to two creatures. Cast it at the end of your opponent's turn, or on your own turn to tap their blockers and attack.
- **Bushwhack:** Early it finds a basic land, which is why the deck has 6 basics. Later it's a 1-mana fight spell with a 5/5. Ram Through does the same thing at instant speed.
- **27 instants and sorceries:** That's enough to power the cost reduction. Consider and Otherworldly Gaze can also put extra spells straight into the graveyard. Otherworldly Gaze can be cast again from the graveyard (flashback).
- **Ledger Shredder:** A 2-mana flyer. It draws and discards whenever a player casts their second spell in a turn, which also fills the graveyard. Brazen Borrower adds flash pressure and a bounce spell.
- **Watch out:** Brazen Borrower is a creature card in the graveyard, so its bounce half doesn't count toward the cost reduction.
- **Odds:** With no mulligans, you have a 79% chance of seeing at least one Terror or Crab by turn 4 on the play. You'll almost always have a cheap spell by then (99.8%).

**The mana**
- You get 17 blue sources and 15 green. That's in line with Izzet Prowess, another low-curve spells deck (about 19.7 lands and 16.4 blue sources on average).
- I ran 19 lands. The deck checker suggested 23, but it counts Terror and Crab as full 7-drops, and in practice they cost 1–3.
- The checker also flagged "0 red sources." That only came from comparing against Izzet Prowess and doesn't apply here.

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Aether Gust
- 2 Mystical Dispute
- 2 Pick Your Poison
- 2 Tishana's Tidebinder
- 2 Tormod's Crypt
- 2 Negate
- 2 Essence Scatter

**How to sideboard**
- **Mono-Red and Izzet Prowess:** Bring in Aether Gust. Your 5/5s block their burn-sized creatures well. Take out Spell Pierce and a cantrip.
- **Greasefang (most played, 12.7%):** Bring in Tormod's Crypt, Tishana's Tidebinder (it can counter the Greasefang trigger) and Pick Your Poison. Take out Snakeskin Veil and Quandrix Charm.
- **Golgari Midrange:** Bring in Essence Scatter. Keep Snakeskin Veil and the fight spells, and cut Spell Pierce.
- **Blue-White Control and Dimir decks:** Bring in Mystical Dispute and Negate. Take out Ram Through and Fading Hope.

**What I couldn't verify**
None of these three cards has a real tournament record in Pioneer, so the card counts are reasoned out from the cards themselves rather than proven by results. The likely weak spot is Bushwhack: it does nothing as a fight spell until a big creature has landed. If testing shows that, cut one Bushwhack for a third Ram Through.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Eyetwitch, Stitcher's Supplier and Flare of Malice.
results.text:
I submitted the deck. It's a brew, Rakdos Eyetwitch Sacrifice-Reanimator, and it's legal and passed every check.

**The plan**
Your three cards already show up together in Modern Reanimator: Stitcher's Supplier and Flare of Malice are in all 17 Reanimator lists from the last 90 days. So I borrowed that deck's frame (Persist into Archon of Cruelty) and rebuilt the creature base around Eyetwitch. You play cheap black creatures that want to die, sacrifice them for value, get Archon of Cruelty into the graveyard, and bring it back with Persist on turns 2–3. Flare of Malice is free removal, paid for by sacrificing one of those creatures.

**Why the key cards**
- **Eyetwitch (4):** When it dies, it "learns." You either discard a card to draw a card, or take a Lesson card from your sideboard.
  - The discard half throws Archon of Cruelty away for Persist. That makes it a third way to bin Archon, next to Faithless Looting and Stitcher's Supplier.
  - The Lesson half gives you a 6-card toolbox you can reach in game one, before sideboarding.
- **Viscera Seer (3):** This is the main change from the stock list (it's not normally in Reanimator). Its free "sacrifice a creature: scry 1" lets you kill Eyetwitch whenever you want. Eyetwitch on turn 1, then Seer on turn 2, sacrificing Eyetwitch to discard Archon, sets up Persist that same turn or the next.
- **Stitcher's Supplier (4):** Mills 3 when it enters and again when it dies. That's 6 cards toward finding or binning Archon, from one card.
- **Flare of Malice (4):** 17 creatures can pay its free cost: Eyetwitch, Supplier, Bloodghast, Seer and Orcish Bowmasters. With Supplier it's free removal plus 3 more cards milled. With Eyetwitch it's free removal plus a card.
- **Bloodghast, Village Rites (3), Corrupted Conviction (2):** More sacrifice fodder and card draw. Bloodghast comes back whenever you play a land.
- **To make room** for Eyetwitch and Seer, I cut Detective's Phoenix, Voldaren Epicure and some burn from the stock list.

**Odds** (no mulligans, by turn 3, on the play)
| What you see | Chance |
|---|---|
| At least one of Looting, Eyetwitch or Supplier | 88.7% |
| A creature you can sacrifice to Flare | 96.2% |
| Persist | 48.8% |
| All three together | about 40% |

If Persist doesn't show up, you still have a grindy game with Bloodghast, Bowmasters, Archon on a later Persist, and free removal.

**The mana**
I kept the stock Reanimator mana: 18 lands, 14 black sources and 13 red, which the check matched against real lists. The checker suggests about 20 lands for a generic deck. I stayed at 18 because the deck never pays Archon's 8 mana, and the Lesson-and-Flare tricks need no lands at all.

**Sideboarding against the current meta**
Each Lesson is a single copy that does double duty. You can board it in normally, and Eyetwitch can fetch it mid-game. If you board a Lesson in, Eyetwitch can no longer fetch it.
- **Energy (20.6%), Prowess, Domain Zoo:** Bring in Iroh's Demonstration, Ruinous Waterbending and Brotherhood's End. Leave Firebending Lesson in the sideboard for Eyetwitch to fetch.
- **Affinity (9.4%):** Bring in 2 Brotherhood's End (artifact mode) and Rakdos Charm. Keep Price of Freedom in the sideboard as an Eyetwitch target.
- **Eldrazi Tron, Amulet Titan, Eldrazi Ramp:** Bring in 2 Obsidian Charmaw (it costs less against lands that make colorless mana) and Extract the Truth. Price of Freedom can also kill a land.
- **Goryo's Vengeance, Living End:** Bring in 2 Dauthi Voidwalker and 2 Rakdos Charm (exile their graveyard). Dai Li Indoctrination can take a piece from their hand.
- **Blink and control:** Bring in Dauthi Voidwalker and Extract the Truth. Necrotic Fumes exiles a creature or planeswalker.

**Stock, tuned or brew?**
It's a brew. The engine is the Eyetwitch learn toolbox, which none of the recent results use (0 lists in 90 days), plus the Seer sac outlet. The mana and interaction come from Reanimator.

**What I couldn't verify**
- No tournament results for this exact build exist. How well it does against the field is my estimate, not data.
- I'm assuming Lessons in your sideboard can be fetched by learn in Modern, which is how learn's text reads. Check this with your tournament organizer if your event handles outside-the-game cards differently.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Fight Rigging, Turntimber Symbiosis and Slumbering Trudge.
results.text:
I built and submitted a brew: **Mono-Green Fight Rigging Stompy**. It passed the legality and mana checks with no warnings.

## The plan
Cheap creatures with 6 power (Slumbering Trudge, Pugnacious Hammerskull) need only Fight Rigging's +1/+1 counter to reach the 7 power that lets you play the hidden card for free. Ideally that hidden card is Turntimber Symbiosis, a free 7-mana spell that digs for another fatty. Ouroboroid and Ghalta keep the board growing until you win, around turn 5.

## Why the key cards
- **Slumbering Trudge:** it works two ways.
  - **Turn 1 for X=0:** a 6/6 that enters tapped with three stun counters. Fight Rigging only checks power, not whether the creature is tapped, so this stunned Trudge still turns Rigging on when Rigging lands on turn 2 or 3.
  - **Later for X=3:** with Hierarchs it's an untapped 6/6 for 4 mana.
  - **From Turntimber's dig:** its mana value in the library is 1, so it enters with three extra counters (9/9). It's still stunned, but it powers Rigging.
- **Fight Rigging:** the 26 cards listed in the deck's support notes all help it reach 7 power. That includes Vines of Vastwood (kicked, +4/+4) and Aspect of Hydra, which you can cast in response to Rigging's combat trigger. The power check happens when the trigger resolves, so an instant pump works.
- **Turntimber Symbiosis:** if you cast it, it looks at 7 cards, and most of the creatures here cost 3 or less, so they get +3 counters (Hammerskull becomes a 9/9). Otherwise you play it as a green land, which keeps the land count honest.
- **Pugnacious Hammerskull:** a 6/6 for 3. It gets a stun counter when it attacks without another Dinosaur, and Ghalta is a Dinosaur.
- **Support:**
  - **Ouroboroid:** grows the whole board each combat.
  - **Ghalta:** costs about GG next to two 6-power creatures.
  - **Keen-Eyed Curator:** graveyard hate that becomes a 7/7.
  - **Green Sun's Zenith:** finds whichever creature you're missing.
  - **Bridgeworks Battle:** fight removal that doubles as a land.

**Honest odds:** with no mulligans, you have Fight Rigging by turn 3 on the play only 48.8% of the time. You have it together with a 7-power enabler 44.3% of the time. Without Rigging, the deck still plays as a solid stompy deck with 6/6s on turns 2–3.

## Mana
The mana is borrowed from the Mono-Green Midrange shell: 8 Hierarchs, 16 lands and 6 cards that are spells on one side and lands on the other (4 Turntimber, 2 Bridgeworks). Real Mono-Green Midrange lists run 19.7 lands on average, and the check counted 19 here with 23 green sources. Boseiju, Ba Sing Se and Dryad Arbor (which Green Sun's Zenith can also fetch) are utility lands.

## Sideboarding
| Opponent | In |
|---|---|
| Affinity (9.9%), Mono-Blue Belcher | Force of Vigor ×3, Collector Ouphe, Pick Your Poison |
| Energy (16.6%), Prowess | Dismember ×2, Tail Swipe ×2 |
| Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, Grixis Persist | Endurance ×2, Vexing Bauble ×2 (counters spells cast without spending mana) |
| Storm, Amulet Titan, Eldrazi Tron/Ramp | Damping Sphere ×2, Vexing Bauble |

Take out Aspect of Hydra, a Ghalta and some copies of Vines against decks that don't kill creatures.

You flood the board with free artifacts. Each artifact spell you cast lets Riddlesmith loot (draw a card, then discard one). The discards go straight into the graveyard:
- **Ovalchase Daredevil** comes back to your hand whenever any artifact enters under your control, so it's a 4/2 the opponent can't remove for good.
- **Echo of Eons** gets flashed back for {2}{U} once your hand is empty. You draw a fresh seven, and the opponent's hand and graveyard get shuffled away.

You win with Daredevil beats, Urza's Saga Constructs and an unblockable, growing Kappa Cannoneer.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State.
results.text:
I built and submitted a Grixis (blue-black-red) Phoenix brew. Its fastest start puts three hasty Phoenixes into play on turn 1. The usual plan is to put Phoenixes in the graveyard on turns 2–3 and bring them back with a turn of cheap spells.

**The plan**
Arclight Phoenix returns from your graveyard at the start of combat on any turn you've cast three or more instants and sorceries. This deck fills the graveyard with Buried Alive or Faithless Looting, then fires off one-mana spells to bring back 3/2 hasty fliers turn after turn. Flow State keeps you supplied with spells.

The best opener: Underground Sea → Dark Ritual (spell 1, adds BBB) → Buried Alive for three Phoenixes (spell 2) → Gut Shot paid with 2 life (spell 3). That's 9 flying damage on turn 1. The exact turn-1 trio comes together only about 4% of the time, before mulligans or cantrips. More often you set up on turns 2–3.

**Why the key cards**
- **Buried Alive:** puts up to three Phoenixes in the graveyard in one card, and it counts as one of your three spells. Dark Ritual can cast it on turn 1.
- **Faithless Looting:** a second way to get Phoenixes into the graveyard (discard them). It also counts toward the three spells, and you can cast it again from the graveyard.
- **Gut Shot and Lava Dart:** the spells that close out a turn. Gut Shot costs no mana (pay 2 life). Lava Dart can be cast a second time by sacrificing a Volcanic Island or Badlands, which count as Mountains.
- **Flow State:** with an instant and a sorcery in your graveyard (which happens almost automatically here), it puts two of the top three cards into your hand.
- **Rest of the deck:** Brainstorm, Ponder, Consider and Lightning Bolt are one-mana spells that count toward the Phoenix trigger. Force of Will protects the plan.
- **Odds:** you have about a 75% chance to see Buried Alive or Looting by turn 3 on the play. That's from raw draws alone, before 10 cantrips dig deeper.

**Changes from the obvious list**
The tools showed two cards I'd otherwise have used are banned in Legacy:
- **Gitaxian Probe:** it would have been the free third spell. Gut Shot fills that role.
- **Entomb:** it would have been a one-mana way to put a Phoenix in the graveyard. Looting and Consider cover that.

**Mana**
The mana base comes from Izzet Tempo, but trimmed to 17 lands (13 blue, 10 black, 10 red sources). Izzet Tempo lists run about 19 lands. This deck can run fewer because 28 of its spells cost one mana or less, it has 4 Dark Rituals, and it has no Daze returning lands to your hand. The deck checker recommended about 17. The basic Island helps against Wasteland, and the 8 fetchlands can find any of your dual lands.

**Sideboarding**
- **Dimir/Izzet Tempo:** bring in Pyroblast and Hydroblast (blue and red counterspell/removal) and Fatal Push. Take out Lava Dart and a Consider.
- **Sneak and Show, OmniTell, Doomsday:** bring in Force of Negation and Thoughtseize. Take out Gut Shot and Lava Dart.
- **Tron, Eldrazi:** bring in Consign to Memory to counter colorless spells and triggers, plus Thoughtseize.
- **Reanimator:** bring in Surgical Extraction and Thoughtseize. Graveyard hate doesn't hurt your plan here.
- **Ocelot Aggro, Death and Taxes, Eldrazi Aggro:** bring in Pyroclasm (it's a sorcery, so it counts toward the Phoenix trigger) and Fatal Push.
- **Against graveyard hate:** opponents will bring in cards like Surgical Extraction against you. After sideboarding, lean on hard-casting Phoenix and on Bolt damage rather than going all-in on Buried Alive.

**Label and caveats**
This is a **brew**. Phoenix had 0 Legacy lists in the last 90 days, and Buried Alive appeared in only one Reanimator list, so nothing here has been tested in tournaments. The 17-land count is a judgment call. Opponents' graveyard hate is the deck's biggest weakness.

I built a Boros (red-white) graveyard-value deck, and it was accepted. It's a **brew**: nobody plays these three cards in Pauper right now (0 lists in the last 90 days for each). The mana is loosely based on the Boros Aggro archetype, which has only 3 recent lists.

**The plan**
The Eidolons are 4-mana 2/2s that you sacrifice for an effect: Sandstorm makes a creature unable to block, and Aurora prevents 3 damage. Whenever you cast a multicolored spell, they come back from your graveyard to your hand. Every time one comes back, a card leaves your graveyard, which puts a +1/+1 counter on Spirit Mascot. So the deck runs 22 multicolored spells, plus discard outlets that put Eidolons in the graveyard early. It wins by attacking with a big Mascot while the Eidolons stop blockers and save it in combat. The sample line in the submission finishes around turn 7.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Creatures:** 4 Spirit Mascot, 3 Aurora Eidolon, 4 Sandstorm Eidolon, 4 Lunarch Veteran, 3 Battlegate Mimic, 3 Stonebound Mentor
- **Spells:** 4 Pursue the Past, 3 Thrilling Discovery, 2 Faithless Looting, 4 Lightning Bolt, 2 Fire at Will, 2 Manamorphose, 2 Prismatic Strands, 2 Lava Dart
- **Lands:** 2 Boros Garrison, 4 Wind-Scarred Crag, 6 Mountain, 6 Plains

**Why the key cards**
- **Pursue the Past** is the best card here. You discard an Eidolon to draw two. Later, its flashback is itself a multicolored spell cast from the graveyard. That one cast returns the Eidolon and triggers Mascot twice: once for the Eidolon leaving, once for Pursue leaving.
- **Thrilling Discovery** and **Faithless Looting** are the other ways to discard Eidolons. Thrilling Discovery is also multicolored, and Looting's flashback triggers Mascot.
- **Manamorphose** is red-green, so it counts as multicolored, and it pays for itself and draws a card. It returns an Eidolon for nothing.
- **Fire at Will** is red-white, so it's removal that also counts as multicolored.
- **Stonebound Mentor** and **Battlegate Mimic** are cheap multicolored creatures. Stonebound Mentor lets you look at your top card and keep it or bottom it (scry 1) whenever cards leave your graveyard. Battlegate Mimic becomes a 4/2 first striker whenever you cast a spell that's both red and white, and 20 of the main deck's cards are.
- **Mascot fuel:** Lava Dart (flashback by sacrificing a Mountain), Lunarch Veteran (can be recast from the graveyard as a spirit), and Prismatic Strands (flashback by tapping a white creature) all grow Mascot. Mascot itself is red and white, so it can tap to pay for Strands' flashback.

**Odds (no mulligans)**
- At least one Eidolon by turn 5: about 72%. With 22 multicolored spells, you'll almost always have a way to bring one back (99.6%).
- Mascot plus at least one card that triggers it by turn 3: about 44%.

**Mana**
18 lands, which is above the tool's suggestion of about 17.6. The deck has seven 4-drops and expensive flashbacks, and Looting can discard extra lands.
- 12 white sources and 12 red sources, because most of the key cards need both colors.
- 6 basic Mountains are kept so Lava Dart's flashback works.
- The check flagged that real Boros Aggro lists run about 16 white sources. Those lists are almost all white, and this one isn't, so I kept the even split.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Terror, Faeries, Jeskai Control, UW Familiars (blue decks):** 3 Pyroblast and 2 Red Elemental Blast. Take out Lava Dart and 1–2 Faithless Looting.
- **Madness and Mono-Red Rally:** the 3rd Prismatic Strands. Aurora Eidolon is already strong here because it prevents burn damage. Take out Looting.
- **Elves, Mono-White Aggro, Faeries:** 2 Electrickery.
- **Affinity:** 2 Dust to Dust.
- **Golgari Gardens and Tron (big creatures):** 2 Journey to Nowhere and 1 Destroy Evil.
- **Graveyard decks and Gardens:** 2 Thraben Charm (exiles graveyards, can kill a creature, or destroys an enchantment). Be careful: exiling every graveyard also exiles your own Eidolons.

**Limits**
- No tournament results exist for this combination, so the win rate is untested.
- Several red-white staples you might expect aren't Pauper-legal, according to the tools: Lightning Helix, Boros Charm and Boros Swiftblade. That's why the deck's multicolored spells are less efficient than usual.
- My searches couldn't filter cards by mana cost. There may be other legal red-white gold or hybrid commons I didn't find.

results.text:
I built a Bant (green-white-blue) creature-sacrifice toolbox around your three cards. It passed the legality check and was accepted. It's a **brew**: I borrowed the creature base, Survival, Natural Order and Opposition from the Tradewind Survival archetype (23 recent lists) and added white for Academy Rector, Swords and Altar of Bone.

**The plan**
- Early on, you play mana creatures and Veteran Explorer, then sacrifice Explorer to jump ahead on lands. Those extra lands pay for the five-mana Future Sight, which needs three blue.
- Academy Rector is your enchantment tutor: when it dies, it puts Future Sight, Opposition or Survival of the Fittest straight onto the battlefield.
- You win through card advantage from Future Sight, or by locking the opponent with Opposition. Then Verdant Force, Exalted Angel and the Tradewind Riders finish.

**Why the key cards**
- **Altar of Bone (3):** The glue. Sacrificing Rector to it is a double tutor: Rector puts an enchantment onto the battlefield, and Altar puts a creature in your hand. Sacrificing Explorer gives you two basic lands and still finds a creature.
- **Phyrexian Altar (2) and Phyrexian Tower (1):** Let you sacrifice a creature at any time and get mana back. With Altar of Bone, that's 6 dedicated ways to kill Rector. Rector can also die by blocking or to the opponent's removal.
- **Natural Order (2):** Sacrifices Explorer (it has to be a green creature) and puts Verdant Force or Deranged Hermit onto the battlefield.
- **Opposition (2):** Fixes Explorer's downside. Explorer gives the opponent two basics too, but under Opposition your creatures tap those lands down every turn.
- **Survival of the Fittest (2):** Discard creatures to find Rector or Explorer. Rector can also fetch Survival itself.
- **Odds:** On the play, you have a 91% chance to see Future Sight, Rector, Altar of Bone or Survival by turn 4. You'll have both Rector and an Altar of Bone/Tower by turn 5 only about 31% of the time. That's why Survival, chump blocks and Phyrexian Altar are there to back it up.

**The mana**
- 21 lands plus 6 mana creatures, kept basic-heavy (4 Forest, 3 Island, 1 Plains) so Explorer and the fetch lands have targets.
- Explorer should usually fetch Islands so you can cast Future Sight's three blue.
- Sources: 16 green, 12 blue, 11 white.
- The check said Tradewind Survival lists run more black, red and green sources. That's because their splashes come from City of Brass, which this deck doesn't need.

**Sideboarding**
- **Stiflenought / Standstill (blue counterspell decks):** Bring in 3 Xantid Swarm, 2 Meddling Mage and Mystic Snake. Take out Phyrexian Altar, Wall of Blossoms and the Verdant Force (8 mana is too slow against counterspells).

- **Moneyball Black:** Bring in Meddling Mage and Xantid Swarm, plus the Crypts if their deck relies on its graveyard.

**What I couldn't verify**
- Altar of Bone has no recent tournament results, and Future Sight and Academy Rector each appear in only 2 recent lists. So the core engine hasn't been tested in competition.
- Veteran Explorer is symmetrical and can ramp an opponent like Goblins. Against fast decks, don't sacrifice it until Opposition is on the battlefield or close to it.
